title: Variables — typing drills
description: Type short GDScript lines for a fear meter, a flashlight battery, and a few Inspector tweaks. Spacing is flexible, and a trailing semicolon is fine.

drills.prompt: Declare a float named fear set to 0.0.
drills.hint: Start with var, then the name fear. You can write the type as : float or let Godot infer it with :=.
drills.explain: All of these are valid: var fear: float = 0.0, var fear := 0.0, and var fear = 0.0. Using := or a typed float keeps fear a decimal, which is what a creeping fear meter needs.

drills.prompt: Declare a variable named flashlight_battery set to 100.0.
drills.hint: Use var and the full name flashlight_battery. 100.0 is a float.
drills.explain: flashlight_battery holds how much charge is left. A float lets it drain by fractions as the light stays on.

drills.prompt: Write an @export variable named max_fear set to 100.0.
drills.hint: Put @export on the same line, just before var.
drills.explain: @export puts max_fear in the Inspector so you can tweak the fear cap while you test, without opening the script.

drills.prompt: Declare a constant named MAX_INVENTORY_SLOTS set to 8.
drills.hint: Use const, not var. Constant names are usually written in ALL_CAPS.
drills.explain: const is for values that should not change. Godot reports an error if the code later tries to assign a new value to MAX_INVENTORY_SLOTS.

drills.prompt: Assign 80.0 to an existing variable named flashlight_battery. Do not declare it again.
drills.hint: This is just an assignment. Do not start the line with var.
drills.explain: Once a variable exists, you change it with =. Writing var again would try to declare a second box with the same name.
